query: What review signals predict negative Amazon product satisfaction?

per_column.name: negative_sentiment_words
per_column.rationale: Count of negative sentiment tokens is derived from review text, not from the label; higher counts plausibly signal negative satisfaction. Legitimate predictor computable before knowing the outcome.

per_column.name: positive_sentiment_words
per_column.rationale: Positive lexicon count carries signal toward positive labels; a valid text-derived feature that does not restate the label.

per_column.name: allcaps_word_count
per_column.rationale: All-caps usage often correlates with strong emotion/frustration; a legitimate stylistic predictor of satisfaction polarity.

per_column.name: exclamation_mark_count
per_column.rationale: Exclamation frequency reflects emotional intensity (positive or negative) and is a plausible, non-leaking predictor derived from text.

per_column.name: question_mark_count
per_column.rationale: Questions may signal confusion/dissatisfaction; weak but legitimate text-derived signal, not a restatement of the label.

per_column.name: repeated_punctuation_count
per_column.rationale: Repeated punctuation (!!!, ???) indexes emotional intensity; a valid stylistic predictor independent of the outcome.

per_column.name: title_word_count
per_column.rationale: Title length is a generic structural feature with weak but non-leaking predictive potential; permissible predictor.

per_column.name: content_word_count
per_column.rationale: Review length can correlate with satisfaction (e.g., detailed complaints); generic but legitimate predictor, not a restatement of the label.

per_column.name: comparative_language_count
per_column.rationale: Comparative phrasing (better/worse than) is a meaningful content signal about relative satisfaction; valid text-derived predictor.

per_column.name: investment_complaint_words
per_column.rationale: Domain-specific complaint lexicon count is derived from text and plausibly predicts negative satisfaction; not leakage since it precedes/derives independently of the label.

per_column.name: product_failure_words
per_column.rationale: Failure-term count is a strong, semantically targeted predictor of dissatisfaction, computed from the review content rather than the label.

per_column.name: durability_complaint_words
per_column.rationale: Durability complaint lexicon is a domain-relevant predictor of negative satisfaction; text-derived and non-leaking.

judge.rationale: All added columns are text-derived features computed from title/content and none restate, decompose, or leak the label_pos outcome, so each qualifies as a legitimate predictor. The set combines targeted sentiment/complaint lexicons (negative/positive sentiment, comparative, investment/product-failure/durability complaints) that carry genuine semantic signal about satisfaction, plus stylistic intensity cues (allcaps, exclamation, repeated punctuation). A cluster of generic length/count features (title/content word counts, question marks) adds only marginal leverage. As a set they provide substantial, non-leaking predictive signal beyond the raw id/title/content, warranting a solidly-above-average utility score rather than a top score, since several features are redundant or weak.
